title: Bidirectional BCI safe stimulation limits
bottleneck: Writing information back into the brain (sensory feedback) requires electrical stimulation, but charge-injection limits (Shannon criteria) cap safe stimulation per electrode to avoid tissue damage. Current materials (platinum) allow only tens of microC/cm2; delivering rich, naturalistic sensation needs far more. Bidirectional BCIs are bottlenecked by electrochemistry.
why_it_blocks: Without safe, high-fidelity stimulation, BCIs are read-only: users get no touch, proprioception, or natural feedback, capping prosthetic dexterity and VR neural interfaces. The write path is the missing half.
current_state: Coatings like PEDOT push charge-injection limits higher, and stimulation paradigms are improving. Naturalistic, high-bandwidth, chronic-safe neural stimulation remains out of reach. Safe charge limits force stimulation to stay weak and coarse, far from the rich patterns needed for natural-feeling sensation.
